claim: The mammalian olfactory system bypasses the thalamus, with olfactory receptor neurons projecting directly to the olfactory bulb.
source: The mammalian olfactory system is unique among sensory systems in that it bypasses the thalamus: olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) in the nose project to the olfactory bulb (OB), a forebrain structure containing – in the mouse – approximately 500,000 neurons per hemisphere (Parrish-Aungst et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parrish-Aungst et al., 2007

claim: The mouse olfactory bulb contains approximately 500,000 neurons per hemisphere.
source: The mammalian olfactory system is unique among sensory systems in that it bypasses the thalamus: olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) in the nose project to the olfactory bulb (OB), a forebrain structure containing – in the mouse – approximately 500,000 neurons per hemisphere (Parrish-Aungst et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Parrish-Aungst et al., 2007

claim: OB projection neurons directly project to a variety of cortical structures, including the anterior olfactory nucleus, piriform cortex, cortical amygdala, and the lateral entorhinal cortex.
source: The latter directly project to a variety of cortical structures, including the anterior olfactory nucleus, piriform cortex, cortical amygdala, and the lateral entorhinal cortex (Ghosh et al., 2011; Haberly and Price, 1977; Miyamichi et al., 2011; Sosulski et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations: Ghosh et al., 2011; Haberly and Price, 1977; Miyamichi et al., 2011; Sosulski et al., 2011

claim: Each ORN in the mouse expresses only one of approximately 1000 olfactory receptor genes.
source: Each ORN in the mouse expresses only one of approximately 1000 olfactory receptor genes (Buck and Axel, 1991; Yoshihito, 2012; Zhang and Firestein, 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to Buck and Axel, 1991; Yoshihito, 2012; Zhang and Firestein, 2002

claim: ORNs expressing the same receptor project axons onto defined spherical structures called glomeruli.
source: ORNs expressing the same receptor project axons onto defined spherical structures, glomeruli (Mori and Sakano, 2011), containing a variety of neuropil including the apical dendrites of 10–50 projection neurons (Bartel et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Mori and Sakano, 2011; Bartel et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2018

claim: Glomeruli contain the apical dendrites of 10–50 projection neurons.
source: ORNs expressing the same receptor project axons onto defined spherical structures, glomeruli (Mori and Sakano, 2011), containing a variety of neuropil including the apical dendrites of 10–50 projection neurons (Bartel et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bartel et al., 2015; Schwarz et al., 2018

claim: OB projection neurons have been historically divided into mitral and tufted cells based on soma location and dendritic and axonal projection patterns.
source: Historically, OB projection neurons have been divided into mitral and tufted cells (MCs, TCs), largely based on their soma location and dendritic and axonal projection pattern (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Haberly and Price, 1977; Imamura et al., 2020; Mori et al., 1983; Orona et al., 1984)
evidence: Supported by citations to Haberly and Price, 1977; Imamura et al., 2020; Mori et al., 1983; Orona et al., 1984

claim: MC somata are located predominantly in a thin layer with their dendrites covering the deeper part of the OB external plexiform layer.
source: MC somata are located predominantly in a thin layer with their dendrites covering the deeper part of the OB external plexiform layer.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text

claim: MC axons project to a wide range of structures including posterior piriform cortex.
source: Their axons project to a wide range of structures including posterior piriform cortex.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text

claim: TC axons are restricted to more anterior forebrain structures.
source: TC axons, on the other hand, are restricted to more anterior forebrain structures and their cell bodies are distributed across the external plexiform layer, with dendrites largely restricted to superficial layers.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text

claim: TC cell bodies are distributed across the external plexiform layer, with dendrites largely restricted to superficial layers.
source: TC axons, on the other hand, are restricted to more anterior forebrain structures and their cell bodies are distributed across the external plexiform layer, with dendrites largely restricted to superficial layers.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text

claim: Within the TC population, subdivisions have been made into deep, middle, superficial, and external TCs, largely based on soma position.
source: Within the TC population, subdivisions have been made into deep, middle, superficial, and external TCs, largely based on soma position.
evidence: Direct statement in the manuscript text

claim: TCs respond more readily, with higher peak firing rates, and to lower odor concentration in vivo compared to MCs.
source: Consequently, TCs respond more readily, with higher peak firing rates, and to lower odor concentration in vivo (Griff et al., 2008; Kikuta et al., 2013; Nagayama et al., 2014), and earlier in the respiration cycle compared to MCs (Ackels et al., 2020; Fukunaga et al., 2012; Igarashi et al., 2012; Jordan et al., 2018; Phillips et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Griff et al., 2008; Kikuta et al., 2013; Nagayama et al., 2014

claim: TCs respond earlier in the respiration cycle compared to MCs.
source: Consequently, TCs respond more readily, with higher peak firing rates, and to lower odor concentration in vivo (Griff et al., 2008; Kikuta et al., 2013; Nagayama et al., 2014), and earlier in the respiration cycle compared to MCs (Ackels et al., 2020; Fukunaga et al., 2012; Igarashi et al., 2012; Jordan et al., 2018; Phillips et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ackels et al., 2020; Fukunaga et al., 2012; Igarashi et al., 2012; Jordan et al., 2018; Phillips et al., 2012

claim: A subset of MCs show regular firing, while others show 'stuttering' behavior characterized by irregular action potential clusters.
source: Both in vivo and in vitro recordings suggest that a subset of MCs show regular firing, while others show 'stuttering' behavior characterized by irregular action potential clusters (Angelo et al., 2012; Balu et al., 2004; Bathellier et al., 2008; Buonviso et al., 2003; Carey and Wachowiak, 2011; Desmaisons et al., 1999; Fadool et al., 2011; Friedman and Strowbridge, 2000; Margrie and Schaefer, 2003; Padmanabhan and Urban, 2010; Schaefer et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to in vivo and in vitro recording studies

claim: Cdhr1 and Tbx21 have been shown to be selectively expressed in a subset of OB projection neurons.
source: For OB projection neurons, however, only little information about chemotypes (Kiyokage et al., 2010) is available at this point: Cdhr1 and Tbx21 Haddad et al., 2013; Nagai et al., 2005 have been shown to be selectively expressed in a subset of OB projection neurons.
evidence: Supported by citations to Haddad et al., 2013; Nagai et al., 2005

claim: CCK distinguishes a subset of TCs (superficial TCs).
source: CCK distinguishes a subset of TCs (superficial TCs, [Liu and Shipley, 1994; Seroogy et al., 1985; Short and Wachowiak, 2019; Sun et al., 2020]).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu and Shipley, 1994; Seroogy et al., 1985; Short and Wachowiak, 2019; Sun et al., 2020

claim: Vasopressin-expressing cells might constitute a further subset of superficial TCs.
source: Vasopressin-expressing cells might constitute a further subset of superficial TCs (Lukas et al., 2019)
evidence: Supported by citation to Lukas et al., 2019, with speculative language ('might')

claim: The Lbhd2 gene has been used to obtain more specific genetic access to MCs.
source: and recently, the Lbhd2 gene has been used to obtain more specific genetic access to MCs (Koldaeva et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Koldaeva et al., 2021

claim: The study used viral injections into olfactory cortex and fluorescent nucleus sorting to enrich PNs for high-throughput single nucleus and bulk RNA deep sequencing.
source: Here, we used viral injections into olfactory cortex and fluorescent nucleus sorting to enrich PNs for high-throughput single nucleus and bulk RNA deep sequencing.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental methods used in the study

claim: Transcriptome analysis and RNA in situ hybridization identified distinct mitral and tufted cell populations with characteristic transcription factor network topology, cell adhesion, and excitability-related gene expression.
source: Transcriptome analysis and RNA in situ hybridization identified distinct mitral and tufted cell populations with characteristic transcription factor network topology, cell adhesion, and excitability-related gene expression.
evidence: Direct statement of study findings

claim: Different mitral cell populations preferentially project to different target regions.
source: Finally, we describe a new computational approach for integrating bulk and snRNA-seq data and provide evidence that different mitral cell populations preferentially project to different target regions.
evidence: Direct statement of study findings

claim: A total of 31,703 nuclei were analyzed, grouped in 22 clusters.
source: We analyzed a total of 31,703 nuclei, grouped in 22 clusters that were annotated post hoc based on the expression of established marker genes for excitatory and inhibitory neurons and glial cell populations (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results, with reference to Figure 2A-C

claim: Putative OB projection neurons comprised 23.66% (n = 7504) of all nuclei analyzed.
source: We initially used the combinatorial expression patterns of glutamatergic and previously characterized M/T cell markers (Vglut1, Vglut2, Vglut3, Tbx21, Cdhr1, Thy1) to identify putative OB projection neurons, comprising 23.66% (n = 7504) of all nuclei.
evidence: Direct statement of data analysis results

claim: The study identified three distinct types of MCs (M1, M2, and M3) and five distinct types of TCs (T1, ET1, ET2, ET3, and ET4).
source: Our analysis revealed eight molecularly distinct clusters of putative projection neurons and one cluster of putative periglomerular cells (Figure 2D,E). Among projection neurons, we identified three clusters of MCs (M1, M2, and M3) and five clusters of middle and external TCs (T1, ET1, ET2, ET3, and ET4).
evidence: Direct statement of findings with reference to Figure 2D,E

claim: Kcng1, Lhx5, and Sertm1 were identified as putative M1-specific marker genes.
source: Differential expression (DE) analysis identified the voltage-gated potassium channel Kcng1, the transcriptional regulator LIM homeobox 5 (Lhx5) and the serine-rich transmembrane domain 1 (Sertm1) as putative M1-specific marker genes.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Two-color smFISH revealed extensive co-localization of Kcng1 and Lhx5 transcripts within the same subpopulation of cells in the MC layer.
source: Two-color smFISH revealed extensive co-localization of Kcng1 and Lhx5 transcripts within the same subpopulation of cells in the MC layer (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,R).
evidence: Direct statement of smFISH results with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,R

claim: Piezo2, Vgll2, and Zfp114 were identified as putative M2-specific markers.
source: Next, DE analysis identified the mechanosensory ion channel Piezo2, the transcription cofactor vestigial like family member 2 (Vgll2) and the zinc finger protein 114 (Zfp114) as putative M2-specific markers.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Cadps2, Calca, and Fst were identified as putative M3-specific markers.
source: Finally, we identified the calcium-dependent secretion activator 2 (Cadps2), calcitonin (Calca), and follistatin (Fst) as putative M3-specific markers.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Barhl2, Sgcg, Vdr, Olfr110, and Olfr111 were identified as putative T1 markers.
source: DE analysis for TC type-specific genes identified the transcription factor BarH-like homeobox 2 (Barhl2), the gamma-sarcoglycan Sgcg, the vitamin D receptor (Vdr), and the olfactory receptors Olfr110 and Olfr111 as putative T1 markers.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Coch and Wnt5b were identified as putative ET1 markers.
source: The coagulation factor C homolog (Coch) and the Wnt family member 5b (Wnt5b) were identified as putative ET1 markers.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Lhx1 and Ebf3 were identified as putative ET2 markers.
source: The LIM homeobox 1 (Lhx1) and the early B-cell factor 3 (Ebf3) were identified as putative ET2 markers.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: Ly6g6e and Foxo1 were identified as putative ET4 markers.
source: Finally, we identified the lymphocyte antigen 6 family member 6GE (Ly6g6e) and the transcription factor Forkhead box O1 (Foxo1) as putative ET4 markers.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression analysis results

claim: The study used SCENIC pipeline to infer gene regulatory networks of each type of projection neuron.
source: To infer the regulatory networks of each type of projection neuron, we used the Single-Cell Regulatory Network Inference and Clustering pipeline (SCENIC, Aibar et al., 2017, Van de Sande et al., 2020).
evidence: Direct statement of computational method used, with citations

claim: SCENIC analysis computed 86 regulons with a range of 8–551 target genes (median = 23.5).
source: We applied SCENIC to MCs and TCs (6484 cells), computing 86 regulons with a range of 8–551 target genes (median = 23.5).
evidence: Direct statement of computational analysis results

claim: The 86 regulons grouped into seven modules (mod1–7) based on Connection Specificity Index analysis.
source: By computing the CSI on the basis of pairwise comparisons of regulon activity patterns across cells, we found that the 86 regulons grouped into seven modules (mod1–7) (Figure 4B,C).
evidence: Direct statement of analysis results with reference to Figure 4B,C

claim: The TF network is dominated by three hub genes: Pbx3 (activates 17 TFs), Bclaf1 (activates 11 TFs), and Taf1 (activates 9 TFs).
source: The network is dominated by three hub genes, two of which may self-activate: Pbx3 (activates 17 TFs), Bclaf1 (activates 11 TFs), and Taf1 (activates 9 TFs).
evidence: Direct statement of network analysis results

claim: 55 of the 86 TFs (64%) show possible self-activating regulation.
source: Fifty-five of the 86 TFs (64%) show possible self-activating regulation, and several others form mutually activating pairs (e.g. Lhx1 and Uncx).
evidence: Direct statement of network analysis results

claim: The study devised a novel computational approach to recapitulate the constituent cell types from bulk RNA sequencing data by simulating single-nucleus expression profiles.
source: Given that a substantial fraction of isolated nuclei in our experiments was comprised of granule and periglomerular cells, in addition to projection neurons, we devised a novel computational approach to recapitulate the constituent cell types from bulk RNA sequencing data by simulating single-nucleus expression profiles.
evidence: Direct statement of novel computational method developed

claim: Nuclei were simulated from bulk RNA deep sequencing data using a weighted random sampling of regulons with replacement.
source: Nuclei were simulated from bulk RNA deep sequencing data using a weighted random sampling of regulons with replacement.
evidence: Direct statement of computational method

claim: All M2 and M3 MCs were classified as PCx-simPN by 100% of classifiers, suggesting that these mitral types preferentially project to posterior targets.
source: All M2 and M3 MCs were classified as PCx-simPN by 100% of classifiers, suggesting that these mitral types preferentially project to posterior targets (Figure 6C).
evidence: Direct statement of classification results with reference to Figure 6C

claim: 73.5% of M1 MCs were classified as AON-simPN by at least 80% of classifiers, suggesting that M1 MCs preferentially project to anterior targets.
source: In contrast, 73.5% of M1 MCs were classified as AON-simPN by at least 80% of classifiers, suggesting that M1 MCs preferentially project to anterior targets (Figure 6C).
evidence: Direct statement of classification results with reference to Figure 6C

claim: The vast majority (44 of 57) PCx-projecting mitral cells were classified as M2 cells by at least 80% of classifiers.
source: Consistent with our prediction based on simulated transcriptomes, the vast majority (44 of 57) PCx-projecting mitral cells were classified as M2 cells by at least 80% of classifiers.
evidence: Direct statement of validation results from targeted snRNA-seq experiment

claim: Only 6 of 57 PCx-projecting mitral cells were classified as M1 cells.
source: In contrast, only 6 of 57 PCx-projecting mitral cells were classified as M1 cells
evidence: Direct statement of validation results from targeted snRNA-seq experiment

claim: Observing 44 or more M2 cells in the sn-PCx population would be unlikely if M2 cells were present at the same rate as in the general mitral cell population (binomial test, p=0.001).
source: Were M2 cells present in the sn-PCx population at the same rate as in the general mitral cell population, observing this many or more M2 cells would be unlikely (binomial test, p=0.001, see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: Direct statement of statistical test results

claim: The scarcity of M1 neurons in the sn-PCx population would be unlikely if M1 cells were present at the same rate as the general mitral population (binomial test, p=5.57e-05).
source: Similarly, the scarcity of M1 neurons would be unlikely if M1 cells were present in the sn-PCx mitral population at the same rate as the general mitral population (binomial test, p=5.57e-05).
evidence: Direct statement of statistical test results

claim: The Kcng1 gene encodes for a voltage-gated potassium channel, which forms heterotetrameric channels with the ubiquitously expressed delayed rectifying Kv2.1 potassium channel.
source: The Kcng1 gene encodes for a voltage-gated potassium channel, which forms heterotetrameric channels with the ubiquitously expressed delayed rectifying Kv2.1 potassium channel (indeed also expressed in the M1 cluster) and modifies the kinetics of channel activation and deactivation (Kramer et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kramer et al., 1998

claim: Voltage-gated potassium channels exhibiting prominent differential expression levels in MC and TC subtypes include Kcnd3, Kcng1, Kcnh5, Kcnq3, Kcnj2 and 6, and Hcn1.
source: Other voltage-gated potassium channels exhibiting prominent differential expression levels in MC and TC subtypes include Kcnd3, Kcng1, Kcnh5, Kcnq3, Kcnj2 and 6, and Hcn1 (for details see accompanying website link in Materials and methods).
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression findings

claim: A large number of cell adhesion and axon guidance genes known to control the formation and maintenance of neuronal connectivity were differentially expressed in OB projection neuron types.
source: We also found that a large number of cell adhesion and axon guidance genes known to control the formation and maintenance of neuronal connectivity were differentially expressed in OB projection neuron types.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression findings

claim: Differentially expressed cell adhesion genes include members of the cadherin superfamily (Cdh6, 7, 8 c, 9, 13, and 20).
source: Examples include members of the cadherin superfamily of cell adhesion glycoproteins (Cdh6, 7, 8 c, 9, 13, and 20)
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression findings

claim: Differentially expressed axon guidance genes include components of the Semaphorin/Neuropilin/Plexin complexes, including Nrp1, Nrp2, Plexna3, Sema3e, and Sema5b.
source: and components of the Semaphorin/Neuropilin/Plexin complexes, including Nrp1, Nrp2, Plexna3, Sema3e, and Sema5b.
evidence: Direct statement of differential expression findings

claim: Semaphorin/Neuropilin/Plexin complexes are known to play critical roles in the development and maintenance of neuronal connections, including in OB MCs.
source: Semaphorin/Neuropilin/Plexin complexes are known to play critical roles in the development and maintenance of neuronal connections, including in OB MCs (Inokuchi et al., 2017; Saha et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Inokuchi et al., 2017; Saha et al., 2007

claim: Injection of rAAVretro-CAG-H2B-GFP into PCx and AON resulted in GFP-expressing nuclei located in the mitral cell, external plexiform, glomerular, and granule cell layers.
source: Injection of the virus into PCx and AON resulted in GFP-expressing nuclei located in the mitral cell (empty arrowheads), external plexiform, glomerular (white arrowheads), and granule cell layers
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 1B showing histological validation

claim: Injection of rAAVretro-CAG-H2B-GFP into PCx resulted in GFP-expressing nuclei located in the mitral cell layer.
source: injection into PCx resulted in GFP-expressing nuclei located in the mitral cell layer (empty arrowheads)
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 1B showing histological validation

claim: Injection of rAAVretro-CAG-H2B-GFP into AON resulted in GFP-expressing nuclei located in the external plexiform and glomerular layers and granule cell layers.
source: injection into AON resulted in GFP-expressing nuclei located in the external plexiform and glomerular layers (white arrowheads) and granule cell layers.
evidence: Direct statement with reference to Figure 1B showing histological validation

claim: After quality control, a total of 31,703 nuclei were retained for analysis (median of 2300 genes per nucleus).
source: We retained a total of 31,703 nuclei (median of 2300 genes per nucleus; for each replicate median genes per nucleus: R1 = 2,266; R2 = 2419; R3 = 2,322).
evidence: Direct statement of data processing results

claim: For the sn-PCx dataset, 74 nuclei were retained after quality control (median genes per nucleus: 6,092).
source: For the sn-PCx dataset, we retained a total of 74 nuclei (median genes per nucleus: 6,092).
evidence: Direct statement of data processing results

claim: Male and female C57Bl/6 mice (6–8 weeks old) were used in this study.
source: Male and female C57Bl/6 mice (6–8 weeks old) were used in this study and obtained by in-house breeding.
evidence: Direct statement of experimental subjects

claim: All animal protocols were approved by the Ethics Committee of the board of the Francis Crick Institute and the United Kingdom Home Office under the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986.
source: All animal protocols were approved by the Ethics Committee of the board of the Francis Crick Institute and the United Kingdom Home Office under the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986 (project license number PA2F6DA12), as well as Brown University's Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (protocol number: 21-03-0004) followed by the guidelines provided by the National Institutes of Health.
evidence: Direct statement of ethical approval

claim: TCs preferentially target anterior olfactory regions, including the Anterior Olfactory Nucleus (AON), while MCs target anterior and posterior olfactory areas.
source: TCs preferentially target anterior olfactory regions, including the Anterior Olfactory Nucleus (AON), while MCs target anterior and posterior olfactory areas (Imamura et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Imamura et al., 2020

claim: Regulon activity suggested the existence of distinct subtypes within mitral and tufted cell types.
source: Interestingly, regulon and module activity were not uniform within cell types. Rather, regulon activity suggested the existence of distinct subtypes within mitral and tufted cell types (Figure 4D).
evidence: Direct statement of analysis results with reference to Figure 4D

claim: Hierarchical clustering identified four subtypes of M1, three subtypes each of M2, T1, and ET2, and two subtypes of ET1 and ET4.
source: We used hierarchical clustering to further subdivide cell types, finding four subtypes of M1, three subtypes each of M2, T1, and ET2, and two subtypes of ET1 and ET4.
evidence: Direct statement of clustering analysis results

claim: M1 and ET2 are characterized by the hub Pbx3.
source: For instance, we find that M1 and ET2 are characterized by the hub Pbx3.
evidence: Direct statement of network analysis results

claim: M1 uses Egr1 and Dlx5 with Pbx3, whilst ET2 has a 2-cycle involving Lhx1 and Uncx.
source: Yet both cell types are distinguishable by other TFs: M1 uses Egr1 and Dlx5 with Pbx3, whilst ET2 has a 2-cycle involving Lhx1 and Uncx, which were both identified as marker genes specific for this cell type (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Direct statement of network analysis results with reference to figures

claim: T1 is characterized by the close-knit group of Bcl11a, Cux1, Cux2, Hlf, and Rcor1, which are all members of module 2.
source: T1 is characterized by the close-knit group of Bcl11a, Cux1, Cux2, Hlf, and Rcor1, which are all members of module 2.
evidence: Direct statement of network analysis results

claim: The estrogen receptors Esrra and Esrrg are in the top 15 of specific regulons for ET1.
source: Interestingly, the estrogen receptors Esrra and Esrrg are in the top 15 of specific regulons for ET1, creating a target-gene-rich three-cycle with Ppargc1a: the second group of TFs.
evidence: Direct statement of regulon specificity analysis results

claim: The molecular subcategorization of MCs may delineate differences in connectivity.
source: These findings suggest that the molecular subcategorization of MCs may delineate differences in connectivity.
evidence: Inference drawn from the classification and connectivity results

claim: The types M1, M2, and M3 were defined by gene expression and regulon activity, but these results suggest that they also describe projection target specificity.
source: The types M1, M2, and M3 were defined by gene expression and regulon activity, but these results suggest that they also describe projection target specificity.
evidence: Inference drawn from integration of molecular and connectivity data

claim: Subtypes of MCs and TCs may share important functional properties, possibly blurring at the transcriptional level the traditional division into tufted and mitral cells as the two major classes of OB projection neurons.
source: Together, these results suggest that subtypes of MCs and TCs may share important functional properties, possibly blurring at the transcriptional level the traditional division into tufted and mitral cells as the two major classes of OB projection neurons.
evidence: Inference and speculation based on network analysis results

claim: The gradients of module activity observed over the MC and TC subtypes theoretically provide a mechanism for generating multiple distinct cellular phenotypes.
source: Moreover, the gradients of module activity that we observed over the MC and TC subtypes theoretically provide a mechanism for generating multiple distinct cellular phenotypes, similar to how morphogenetic gradients allow for spatial patterning and cell differentiation (Wolpert, 1969).
evidence: Speculation based on observed gradients, with citation to Wolpert, 1969 for analogous mechanism

claim: Through non-linear regulatory interactions, gradual differences at the transcriptomic level can be translated into selective expression of functional genes.
source: Through non-linear regulatory interactions, gradual differences at the transcriptomic level can be translated into selective expression of functional genes.
evidence: Inference based on known principles of gene regulation

claim: The samples contained 7504 putative projection neurons compared to current estimates of 10,000–30,000 projection neurons overall per OB.
source: However, our samples contained 7504 putative projection neurons compared to current estimates of 10,000–30,000 projection neurons overall per OB (Nagayama et al., 2014; Richard et al., 2010).
evidence: Direct statement comparing sample size to literature estimates, with citations

claim: Sorting nuclei rather than whole cells is thought to more accurately reflect relative cell-type abundance.
source: Furthermore, we sorted nuclei rather than whole cells, which is thought to more accurately reflect relative cell-type abundance (Habib et al., 2017; Lake et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Habib et al., 2017; Lake et al., 2017

claim: The gene expression profiles described provide critical new tools for refining projection neuron cell type identities by aligning a cell's molecular features with its functional properties.
source: Independent from the number of molecularly distinct neuronal cell types, the gene expression profiles we have described here provide critical new tools for refining projection neuron cell type identities by aligning a cell's molecular features with its functional properties.
evidence: Inference about the utility of the study's findings

claim: The functional diversity of odor responses can be explained, at least in part, by the molecular diversity of OB projection neurons.
source: We propose that this functional diversity can be explained, at least in part, by the molecular diversity of OB projection neurons, a model that can now be tested experimentally.
evidence: Proposed model based on integration of functional and molecular findings

claim: The findings that MC types preferentially target anterior or posterior cortical areas is consistent with recent observations using MAP-seq.
source: Our findings that MC types preferentially target anterior or posterior cortical areas is consistent with recent observations using MAP-seq (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: Comparison of study findings with independent study, supported by citation to Chen et al., 2021

claim: Gene expression and connectivity provide overlapping yet complementary axes for cell-type classification.
source: Our results are consistent with the model that gene expression and connectivity provide overlapping yet complementary axes for cell-type classification (Kim et al., 2020).
evidence: Inference supported by citation to Kim et al., 2020

claim: The prominent hub and cycle-related genes identified may act as candidate master regulators of neuronal function.
source: The prominent hub and cycle-related genes we have identified here may act as candidate master regulators of neuronal function, which can be targeted for experimental validation.
evidence: Speculation about the functional role of identified genes

claim: The data set will be an important resource for the emerging study of the evolution of olfactory neural circuits across species.
source: Our data set will be an important resource for the emerging study of the evolution of olfactory neural circuits across species.
evidence: Inference about the broader utility of the study's findings

claim: The detailed molecular description of mouse OB projection neurons provides an entry point toward understanding the evolution of olfactory sensory processing across species.
source: The detailed molecular description of mouse OB projection neurons presented here provides an entry point toward understanding the evolution of olfactory sensory processing across species.
evidence: Inference about the broader implications of the study's findings
